thread:
alex.m: Hey team — customer running Redwood Private in an air-gapped site. Outbound requests to our hosted API are failing intermittently. App logs show upstream connect timeouts and occasional TLS verify errors. Need help triaging.

sara.p: Thanks. Can you paste the minimal repro steps and whether they use a proxy chain (HTTP proxy vs SOCKS5) or a transparent egress gateway? :thinking:

alex.m: Repro steps below. They've got an outbound HTTP proxy (company-proxy.corp) and sometimes a fallback NAT gateway. App env: REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood.ai, client -> proxy -> internet. Fail pattern: ~30% of requests time out, others succeed. No global internet access otherwise (no-internet/airgap).

alex.m: Command I ran from their bastion:
```
$ curl -v --proxy http://company-proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
* Connected to company-proxy.corp (10.10.10.1) port 8080 (#0)
* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to api.redwood.ai:443
* CONNECT api.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
> CONNECT api.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate verify failed
* SSL: certificate verification failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

jordan.k: That looks like the proxy is doing TLS interception (MITM) and replacing the cert with company's CA which isn't trusted by the client runtime. But timeouts suggest there may also be connection blackholing/round-robin to a secondary egress path. Two tracks to check: cert trust chain and CONNECT passthrough reliability.

infra-oncall: Can you get a tcpdump of the CONNECT/SSL handshake when it fails? Also collect the proxy logs for the CONNECT id. If they have a proxy cluster, one node might be returning 200 but dropping the tunnel mid-stream (observed before with mutated HTTP/1.1 proxies).

alex.m: Asked for tcpdump and proxy logs; they provided proxy pod logs and I grabbed a short pcap. Here's the relevant snippet from the pcap (client->proxy->api):
```
12:03:21.123 IP 10.0.0.5.54321 > 10.10.10.1.8080: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 65535
12:03:21.124 IP 10.10.10.1.8080 > 10.0.0.5.54321: Flags [P.], seq 1:200, ack 512, win 65535
12:03:22.200 IP 10.10.10.1.8080 > 203.0.113.45.443: Flags [S], seq 100, win 64240
12:03:32.201 IP 10.10.10.1.8080 > 203.0.113.45.443: Flags [S], seq 101, win 64240
# repeated SYNs, no SYN-ACK for ~10s then proxy closes the tunnel
```

sara.p: 203.0.113.45 is one of our CDN edge addresses (we gave customers an IP allowlist earlier). If SYNs are sent but no SYN-ACK, the proxy node may be unable to egress to that IP (firewall/NAT issue) or routing blackhole. The intermittent success fits a multi-proxy pool with some nodes allowed and some blocked.

alex.m: They confirmed their firewall only allows a small set of IPs and uses a per-proxy allowlist. Their config lists some IP ranges for Redwood but might be stale.

jordan.k: Two-pronged remediation: 1) Add current Redwood egress IP ranges to their firewall allowlist (see our published IP list). 2) For TLS interception, either deploy the company's CA to the workload truststore or configure the proxy to do TLS passthrough (tunnel CONNECT without MITM) for api.redwood.ai. This is safer for integrity.

alex.m: Asked them to try: update allowlist + enable passthrough for api.redwood.ai. They asked for exact IPs and a quick workaround to unblock while firewall changes roll out.

infra-oncall: Quick workaround: configure proxy to always forward CONNECT for api.redwood.ai to a specific outbound SNAT IP that is already allowed by the firewall. Alternatively, if they can install CA cert quickly, add company CA to the container's OS/JVM truststore (commands below).

infra-oncall: Example: add CA to Debian base image trust store:
```
# copy corp proxy CA to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-proxy.crt
sudo cp corp-proxy.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/
sudo update-ca-certificates
# restart app so JVM picks up new trust anchors
```

alex.m: They tried adding CA to the image + restart; TLS verify error goes away but timeouts persisted for ~10% of traffic. After we requested proxy logs per node, they found one proxy node had an iptables rule that DROPed forwarding to the egress SNAT pool when conntrack hit 100k (policy issue).

sara.p: That explains intermittent blackholes. Action items: (1) customer to patch iptables conntrack threshold or scale proxy nodes; (2) customer to update firewall allowlist to our current published ranges; (3) recommend proxy passthrough for all Redwood endpoints instead of MITM if they can't maintain trust store across many images.

alex.m: Sent an escalation email to their netops with exact IP ranges and the failing proxy node id + conntrack dump. Also included a minimal diagnostic script they can run to validate connectivity: 
```
#!/bin/bash
HOST=api.redwood.ai
IPS=(203.0.113.45 203.0.113.46 203.0.113.47) # sample edge IPs
for ip in "${IPS[@]}"; do
  echo "Testing $ip via proxy"
  curl -v --proxy http://company-proxy.corp:8080 --resolve "${HOST}:443:${ip}" https://${HOST}/v1/health || echo "fail $ip"
done
```

support-bot: Added priority:high tag and created ticket INF-5021. Assigned to infra-oncall. :white_check_mark:

jordan.k: If they need a longer-term solution, we can offer to set up a dedicated Redwood Dedicated egress IP range for their VPC/private deployment so they only need to allow a few static IPs. I'll follow up with sales/solutions.

alex.m: Thanks all — will close once customer confirms firewall + conntrack fixes. Posting this thread to the case notes. :thumbsup:
